name: API Gateway & Layer 7 Protocols
tagline: Terminating external Layer 7 traffic (HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSockets) at the edge for auth, rate limiting, and protocol translation.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of API Gateways—from L7 protocol termination and gRPC transcoding to avoiding connection pinning and monolithic bottlenecks.

spark.summary: An API gateway terminates external Layer 7 traffic (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSockets) at the edge, centralizing TLS termination, rate limiting, auth verification, and protocol translation before routing to internal services.
spark.keyTakeaway: Centralize cross-cutting edge concerns in a single L7 proxy, but keep business logic out of it so the gateway never becomes a monolithic bottleneck.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** An **API gateway** is a reverse proxy operating at **OSI Layer 7 (Application Layer)**.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Layer 7 API Gateway Request & Protocol Routing Pipeline (Edge Client -> L7 Gateway (Envoy) -> gRPC / REST Pool -> WebSocket Pool); HTTP/2 gRPC Transcoding & Per-RPC Upstream Balancing (Browser (JSON) -> Envoy Gateway -> gRPC Pod 1 -> gRPC Pod 2); Gateway Pod Graceful Drain & Keepalive State Machine (SERVING -> DRAINING -> TERMINATED).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Compare connection models, payload formats, and load-balancing requirements across L7 protocols. Production platforms pair an **Envoy edge gateway** with **per-domain BFF services** and graceful `GOAWAY` draining during rolling deploys.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Dive into gRPC L7 balancing, keepalive timeout alignment, and preventing cascading gateway timeouts.

learningJourney.title: What is an API Gateway
learningJourney.explanation: An **API gateway** is a reverse proxy operating at **OSI Layer 7 (Application Layer)**. Unlike a Layer 4 load balancer that forwards raw TCP/UDP packets by IP and port, an L7 gateway parses HTTP headers, paths, cookies, gRPC metadata, and WebSocket upgrade handshakes—terminating TLS 1.3 once at the edge, validating JWTs against a cached JWKS, enforcing token-bucket rate limits, and transcoding REST/JSON to internal gRPC/Protobuf.

sectionDiagram.title: Layer 7 API Gateway Request & Protocol Routing Pipeline

cards.label: TLS & ALPN Termination
cards.detail: Terminates external TLS 1.3 once at the edge and reuses long-lived HTTP/2 pools upstream.

cards.label: Local Auth & Rate Limit
cards.detail: Verifies JWT signatures against cached JWKS and checks token buckets before forwarding.

cards.label: Protocol Transcoding
cards.detail: Translates browser REST/JSON into internal binary gRPC frames using .proto descriptors.

sectionDiagram.summary: An L7 gateway terminates edge protocols once and routes stateless RPCs and stateful sockets to isolated upstream pools.

learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how an API Gateway works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why we need L7 Gateways (and why L4 proxies break gRPC)
learningJourney.explanation: **Layer 4 load balancers break HTTP/2 and gRPC**: because gRPC multiplexes thousands of RPCs over *one* long-lived TCP connection, an L4 proxy pins all RPCs from a client onto a single backend pod. Gateways also prevent **WebSocket reconnect storms**, **buffer bloat** on large uploads, and **timeout mismatches** between REST (5s) and WebSocket routes (60s+ idle).

sectionDiagram.title: HTTP/2 gRPC Transcoding & Per-RPC Upstream Balancing
sectionDiagram.summary: Terminating HTTP/2 at the L7 gateway lets it balance individual gRPC streams across all backend pods.

ideas.title: Strip Untrusted Edge Headers
ideas.description: Always overwrite X-User-* and untrusted X-Forwarded-For hops at the outermost listener to prevent header spoofing.

ideas.title: Retry Budgets <= 20%
ideas.description: Allow automatic retries only on idempotent GET/HEAD requests, bounded to <=20% of active traffic.

learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without L7 Gateways under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Where API Gateways fit (and when to split BFFs)
learningJourney.explanation: Use an API gateway at the **north-south ingress boundary** for cross-cutting concerns; split UI aggregation into a BFF and high-volume `/ws` sockets into a dedicated pool.

benefits: Centralizes TLS, WAF, JWKS auth, rate limiting, and observability (X-Request-ID).
costs: Adds 1–3 ms proxy hop; misconfigured plugins affect all routes globally.

benefits: Isolates memory-heavy persistent sockets from latency-sensitive REST/gRPC workers.
costs: Requires gradual connection draining (5–10 min) + jittered client reconnects on deploy.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Domain Business Logic in Gateway Plugins
benefits: Move fan-out joins and DB lookups into a separate Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) service.
costs: Heavy Lua/Wasm orchestration turns the gateway into an unmaintainable monolith.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How Gateway Timeouts, Pools, and Rate Limits are managed
learningJourney.explanation: Separate timeouts by route (`5s` for REST/gRPC, `60s` idle for WebSockets), enable `h2`/`h2c` upstream pools, and align keepalive timeouts.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```yaml
# Envoy / Gateway route policy separating REST/gRPC timeouts from WebSockets
routes:
  - match: { prefix: "/v2/payments" }
    route:
      cluster: payments_grpc_h2
      timeout: 5s
      retry_policy:
        retry_on: "connect-failure,reset"
        num_retries: 1
  - match: { prefix: "/ws/ticker" }
    route:
      cluster: ws_stateful_pool
      timeout: 0s
      idle_timeout: 60s
      upgrade_configs:
        - upgrade_type: websocket
```
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: REST vs. gRPC vs. WebSockets
learningJourney.explanation: Compare connection models, payload formats, and load-balancing requirements across L7 protocols.

benefits: Native browser support, human-readable, cacheable via ETag/Cache-Control.
costs: Verbose JSON parsing and larger payloads at high RPS.

benefits: 5–10x smaller binary payloads, strict .proto contracts, bidirectional streaming.
costs: Requires L7 stream balancing and grpc-web/JSON transcoding for browsers.

benefits: Full-duplex persistent TCP tunnel for real-time tickers, chat, and collaboration.
costs: Sticky per-connection state; vulnerable to thundering-herd reconnects on deploy.

supportingConcepts.title: Problem: gRPC & HTTP/2 L7 Load Balancing

learningJourney.purpose: Applied problems: connect these internals to concrete system design and debugging scenarios.

knowledgeCheck.question: You place a Layer 4 Network Load Balancer in front of 10 gRPC backend pods. During a traffic spike, 1 pod hits 100% CPU while 9 pods sit idle. Why?

options.text: gRPC multiplexes all RPCs over a single long-lived HTTP/2 TCP connection, which L4 pins to one pod
options.feedback: Correct: L4 balances per TCP connection, not per HTTP/2 stream; you need an L7 proxy (e.g. Envoy) to balance individual gRPC requests.
Protobuf is only the payload format; the bottleneck is L4 TCP connection pinning.

options.text: gRPC requires sticky sessions via cookies
options.feedback: gRPC is stateless per-RPC and does not use HTTP cookies.

**Why Beginners Should Care:** Centralize cross-cutting edge concerns in a single L7 proxy, but keep business logic out of it so the gateway never becomes a monolithic bottleneck.
